explanation: The left hand is traditionally considered unclean in Indonesia because it's associated with personal hygiene, so it should be avoided for eating, passing food, and giving or receiving items. This norm is especially strong given Indonesia's Muslim-majority population, where similar left-hand taboos are widespread. Visitors eating with their hands (common at many local meals) should use the right hand only.
local_tip: Eat, pass dishes, and hand over money or gifts with your right hand; if you must use your left hand, a quick 'maaf, tangan kiri' (sorry, left hand) smooths it over.

also_check.note: The left hand is reserved for bathroom hygiene; always eat and pass items with the right hand.
The left hand is strictly avoided for eating and greeting; the right hand is used for all such interactions.
There's no left-hand taboo, but chopstick etiquette and other table manners matter more.

sources.title: Why visitors to Indonesia should avoid using their left hand
